We are writing to inform you of a new investment in Pinterest (the "Company"), a visual discovery and bookmarking platform that lets users organize images they find interesting onto themed boards.
We have committed USD 10 million in the Company's Series A at a pre-money valuation of USD 40 million, for approximately 20% on a fully-diluted basis.
What attracted us was the user engagement profile.

Users return roughly six times per week on average, and 68% remain active 30 days after first signup.

These are exceptional engagement metrics for a consumer product at this stage.
The Company's user base is unusual in two respects.
First, 82% of active users are women — an unusually high concentration.
Second, the user base skews older than typical social products, with heaviest concentration in the 25-44 age range.

This combination — engaged users, female-skewed, older demographic — represents a strong and underserved advertising audience and supports a credible long-term monetization path through native advertising in categories such as home decor, fashion, and weddings.

The exit of NorTech Industries — which closed in January 2026 at SEK 18.4 billion and generated a 3.56x gross MOIC / 31.4 percent gross IRR — is the largest realisation in the Fund's history and the principal driver of the Fund's current returns trajectory.
Across the remaining eight active portfolio companies, performance has been broadly positive with two notable challenges.

Helvetia Precision Components, acquired in June 2025, is six months into the hold and tracking modestly ahead of underwriting; the recently-acquired Lumen Specialty Chemicals is on track with its 100-day plan; Brightway Industrial Coatings has had a strong 2025 with revenue and EBITDA growing 14 percent and 21 percent respectively; Eltex Power Systems has performed exceptionally, with revenue growing 23 percent and EBITDA growing 31 percent year-on-year supported by an order backlog that has grown from EUR 285 million at acquisition to EUR 480 million today.
Continental Plastics, acquired in March 2023, has had a more difficult 2025 with revenue growth of only 4 percent against an underwriting of 9 percent and broadly flat EBITDA.

We have responded with operational changes including a new Chief Operating Officer and a structured cost reduction programme targeting EUR 22 million of annualised savings; early progress is encouraging but the realisation timeline has lengthened by approximately 12 months.

Drift Logistics, our 2024 third-party logistics investment, faces a softer parcel volume environment (European parcel volumes down 3 percent year-on-year); the Company has nevertheless gained share, with revenue up 6 percent, but EBITDA margins have compressed from 14 to 12 percent.

rows.statementText: Portfolio ESG performance has continued to mature.
All eight active portfolio companies have completed or are in the final stages of SBTi submission.
Absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions reduced 8 percent during 2025 despite portfolio revenue growth of approximately 12 percent.

Female representation in senior leadership across the portfolio reached 34 percent by year-end, up from 28 percent at the start of the year and 22 percent at fund inception, against a 40 percent target by 2027.
We expect two further realisations during 2026.
Brightway Industrial Coatings and Eltex Power Systems are both progressing toward exit-readiness, with formal processes likely to launch in the first and third quarters respectively.

rows.statementText: We are pleased to announce the final close of Meridian European Industrials Fund V at hard cap, with total commitments of EUR 4.8 billion.
Fund V is the largest fund in Meridian's history, representing a meaningful step-up from Fund IV which closed at EUR 3.2 billion in 2021.
The fundraise was completed in eleven months from first close, well ahead of the original eighteen-month target.
Demand exceeded the hard cap by approximately EUR 1.2 billion.

Re-up rates from existing LPs were strong at 96 percent by capital, and the Fund welcomed new investors across three of the largest US public pension funds, two Asian sovereign wealth funds, and a number of European and North American family offices and endowments.
The LP base spans 92 institutional investors across 26 countries.
Fund V will be deployed across European industrial sectors with a particular focus on advanced manufacturing, energy transition, and specialty chemicals.
We anticipate 10 to 12 platform investments over the four-year deployment period, with typical equity tickets in the EUR 300 to 700 million range.
Our investment team has been preparing Fund V's pipeline for many months and we expect first capital calls in the second quarter of 2026.
Meridian Capital has agreed to acquire Project Atlas, a Nordic battery storage platform.
Project Atlas is exceptionally well positioned in the Nordic energy storage market.
James Ortiz, former Chief Executive Officer of GridCo Industries, advised Meridian Capital on the transaction structure.
James Ortiz said, "Project Atlas will double in value within two years."
The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of 2026.
